strings.name: Jerome Powell
strings.role: Central banker · Former Federal Reserve chair
strings.summary: Powell studied politics at Princeton and law at Georgetown, then worked as a lawyer, investment banker, Treasury official and private-equity partner. He joined the Federal Reserve Board in 2012 and served as chair from 2018 to 2026, leading policy discussions during the pandemic and high inflation. Rate cuts, asset purchases and rate increases were collective committee decisions. He remained a governor after leaving the chair in May 2026.
strings.coverageNote: Selected milestones verifiable through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: He led the US Federal Reserve and participated in monetary policy decisions during the pandemic shock and the rise in inflation.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Washington, D.C., United States; born in February 1953.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Princeton politics bachelor’s degree (1975); Georgetown law degree (1979).
strings.highlights.h1.title: Monetary policy in crisis
strings.highlights.h1.text: As chair he led FOMC deliberations; the committee cut rates and purchased assets to support markets during the pandemic shock.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Response to high inflation
strings.highlights.h2.text: From 2022 he led the committee’s shift to rate increases amid trade-offs involving price stability, employment and financial conditions.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Leaves chair, remains governor
strings.timeline.t1.text: Kevin Warsh succeeded him as chair; Powell remained a governor, whose term is separate from the chairmanship.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Begins rate-increase cycle
strings.timeline.t2.text: Under his chairmanship, the FOMC raised the federal funds target range to 0.25%–0.50%, beginning a cycle aimed at inflation.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Emergency pandemic easing
strings.timeline.t3.text: The FOMC cut its target range to 0%–0.25% and announced purchases of Treasury and agency mortgage-backed securities.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Becomes Federal Reserve chair
strings.timeline.t4.text: After years as a governor, he became Board chair and also chaired the Federal Open Market Committee.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Joins Federal Reserve Board
strings.timeline.t5.text: He was sworn in as a governor to fill an unexpired term and was reappointed in 2014.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Becomes Carlyle partner
strings.timeline.t6.text: He became a partner at the Carlyle Group, serving until 2005 and gaining private-equity experience.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Earns law degree
strings.timeline.t7.text: He earned his Georgetown law degree after serving as law journal editor-in-chief, then worked in law.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Graduates from Princeton
strings.timeline.t8.text: He earned a Princeton bachelor’s degree in politics before pursuing legal training.
